questions.questionText: A data set of 8 observations has Σx = 96 and Σx² = 1,280. Calculate (a) the mean x̄ and (b) the unbiased sample variance s² and standard deviation s. [4 marks]

Events A and B satisfy P(A) = 0.45, P(B) = 0.30, and P(A ∪ B) = 0.60.
(a) Find P(A ∩ B). [2 marks]
(b) Determine whether A and B are independent. [2 marks]

A factory produces light bulbs of which 4% are defective. A quality inspector tests a random sample of 12 bulbs (X ~ B(12, 0.04)).
(a) Find P(X = 0). [2 marks]
(b) Find the probability that at least 2 bulbs are defective. [3 marks]

Calls arrive at a Harare helpdesk at a mean rate of 3.2 calls per 10 minutes following a Poisson distribution.
(a) Find the probability of receiving exactly 2 calls in a 10-minute period. [2 marks]
(b) Find the probability of receiving at least 1 call in a 5-minute period. [3 marks]

Marks in an exam follow N(65, 10²).
(a) Find the probability that a randomly chosen candidate scores above 80. [2 marks]
(b) Find the mark required to place in the top 5% (z = 1.645). [2 marks]

A random variable X has probability distribution P(X=x) = kx for x = 1, 2, 3, 4.
(a) Find constant k. [2 marks]
(b) Calculate E(X) and Var(X). [4 marks]

How many distinct 4-digit PIN numbers can be formed from digits {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6} if:
(a) digits may be repeated, [2 marks]
(b) no digit may be repeated and the PIN must be even? [3 marks]
questions.explanation:
(a) 6⁴ = 1,296 [2].
(b) Last digit even ({2,4,6}): 3 choices; remaining 3 positions: 5 × 4 × 3 = 60 -> total = 3 × 60 = 180 [3].

questions.questionText: A committee of 5 learners is chosen from 6 girls and 4 boys. Find the probability that the committee contains exactly 3 girls and 2 boys. [4 marks]

Test 2% of machine parts fail inspection. At factory A (40% output), defect rate is 3%; at factory B (60% output), defect rate is 1%. Given a randomly chosen part is defective, find the probability it came from factory A (Bayes' theorem). [4 marks]

Continuous random variable X has PDF f(x) = c(4 - x²) for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2, and 0 elsewhere.
(a) Show that c = 3/16. [2 marks]
(b) Find E(X). [3 marks]
In a geometric distribution X ~ Geo(0.25) counting trials until first success, find (a) P(X = 4), (b) P(X > 3), and (c) E(X). [4 marks]
Two independent random variables have X ~ N(20, 4) and Y ~ N(12, 5). Find the distribution of W = 2X - Y and calculate P(W > 30). [4 marks]
State three properties of a well-designed stratified random sampling plan and explain when it outperforms simple random sampling. [4 marks]
questions.explanation: Population divided into non-overlapping homogeneous strata (e.g., Form 1–6 or rural/urban); sample drawn randomly from each stratum proportional to stratum size [2]. Outperforms SRS when distinct subgroups vary sharply, preventing under-representation and lowering sampling variance [2].

questions.questionText: Use a normal approximation with continuity correction for X ~ B(100, 0.20) to estimate P(X ≤ 24). [4 marks]
Data set has Q₁ = 32, Median = 45, Q₃ = 54. Calculate the interquartile range and check mathematically if x = 90 is an outlier using the 1.5×IQR fence rule. [4 marks]
questions.explanation: IQR = 54 - 32 = 22 [1]. Upper fence = Q₃ + 1.5(IQR) = 54 + 1.5(22) = 54 + 33 = 87 [2]. Since 90 > 87, yes, x = 90 is an upper outlier [1].

questions.questionText: Cumulative distribution function of X is F(x) = x²/9 for 0 ≤ x ≤ 3. Find the median m and the PDF f(x). [3 marks]
Explain the Central Limit Theorem (CLT) and use it to find the probability that the sample mean x̄ of n = 64 observations from a skewed distribution (μ = 50, σ = 16) exceeds 53. [4 marks]
questions.explanation: For large n (≥30), x̄ is approximately Normal N(μ, σ²/n) regardless of population shape [2]. Standard error = 16/√64 = 2. Z = (53 - 50)/2 = 1.5 -> P(Z > 1.5) = 0.0668 [2].

questions.questionText: Independent Poisson variables X ~ Po(2.4) and Y ~ Po(1.6) represent defects from two machines. Find P(X + Y ≤ 2). [3 marks]
In Spearman's rank correlation on 6 paired observations, Σd² = 8. Calculate r_s and comment on the association. [3 marks]
questions.explanation: r_s = 1 - 6Σd² / [n(n² - 1)] = 1 - 48 / (6 × 35) = 1 - 48/210 = 1 - 0.2286 = 0.771 [2]. Indicates strong positive monotonic correlation [1].

questions.questionText: A coin is tossed repeatedly until 2 heads occur, OR until 4 tosses have been made. Construct the probability distribution of X (number of tosses). [4 marks]
